cards.front: In X-linked (Bruton) agammaglobulinemia, what is defective and why do infections start after about 6 months of age?
cards.back: A **BTK** (Bruton tyrosine kinase) defect stops pre-B cells from maturing, so mature **B cells are absent** and all immunoglobulins are very low. Infections begin when **maternal IgG** fades: encapsulated bacteria, enteroviruses and *Giardia*. Tonsils are tiny.
cards.back_pt: Um defeito da **BTK** (tirosina quinase de Bruton) impede a maturação das células pré-B, então os **linfócitos B maduros estão ausentes** e todas as imunoglobulinas são muito baixas. As infecções começam quando a **IgG materna** desaparece: bactérias encapsuladas, enterovírus e *Giardia*. As tonsilas são muito pequenas.

cards.front: How does common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) differ from X-linked agammaglobulinemia?
cards.back: In **CVID**, B cells are **present** but fail to become **plasma cells**, so IgG and IgA are low (IgM in about half). It affects both sexes and usually appears **after childhood**. Risks: recurrent sinopulmonary infections, **autoimmune disease**, granulomas and **lymphoma**.
cards.back_pt: Na **IDCV** (imunodeficiência comum variável), os linfócitos B estão **presentes**, mas não se diferenciam em **plasmócitos**; assim, IgG e IgA ficam baixas (IgM em cerca de metade dos casos). Afeta ambos os sexos e costuma surgir **após a infância**. Riscos: infecções sinopulmonares recorrentes, **doença autoimune**, granulomas e **linfoma**.

cards.front: What is the defect and the antibody pattern in the most common form of hyper-IgM syndrome?
cards.back: X-linked loss of **CD40 ligand** on activated helper T cells. B cells cannot **class switch**: IgM normal or high; **IgG, IgA and IgE low**. CD40L also activates macrophages, so *Pneumocystis*, *Cryptosporidium* and CMV infections occur, along with pyogenic infections.
cards.back_pt: Perda, ligada ao X, do **ligante de CD40** (CD40L) nos linfócitos T auxiliares ativados. Os linfócitos B não fazem **troca de classe**: IgM normal ou alta; **IgG, IgA e IgE baixas**. O CD40L também ativa macrófagos, então ocorrem infecções por *Pneumocystis*, *Cryptosporidium* e CMV, além de infecções piogênicas.

cards.front: What causes autosomal dominant hyper-IgE (Job) syndrome, and what are its key features?
cards.back: A **STAT3** mutation blocks **Th17** differentiation, so neutrophils are poorly recruited. Features: "**cold**" (non-inflamed) *S. aureus* abscesses, **retained primary teeth**, eczema, coarse face, fractures after minor trauma and **very high IgE**.
cards.back_pt: Uma mutação em **STAT3** bloqueia a diferenciação **Th17**, então o recrutamento de neutrófilos é fraco. Achados: abscessos "**frios**" (sem inflamação) por *S. aureus*, **retenção dos dentes decíduos**, eczema, fácies grosseira, fraturas após traumas leves e **IgE muito alta**.

cards.front: Which infections suggest a defect in the IL-12 receptor or the IFN-γ receptor?
cards.back: **Disseminated mycobacterial infections** (including **BCG** after vaccination and nontuberculous mycobacteria) and ***Salmonella***. Macrophages need the IL-12 to IFN-γ loop (Th1) to kill intracellular microbes.
cards.back_pt: **Infecções micobacterianas disseminadas** (incluindo **BCG** após vacinação e micobactérias não tuberculosas) e ***Salmonella***. Os macrófagos precisam da alça IL-12 → IFN-γ (Th1) para matar micróbios intracelulares.

cards.front: What are the most common causes of SCID and how does it present?
cards.back: Most often **X-linked**: a defect in the **IL-2 receptor common γ chain**. Autosomal recessive: **ADA deficiency** (see nucleotide metabolism block). Infants have thrush, chronic diarrhea, failure to thrive, *Pneumocystis* and **no thymic shadow**. Live vaccines are contraindicated.
cards.back_pt: Mais comum: **ligada ao X**, defeito na **cadeia γ comum do receptor de IL-2**. Autossômica recessiva: **deficiência de ADA** (ver bloco de metabolismo dos nucleotídeos). Lactentes têm candidíase oral, diarreia crônica, déficit de crescimento, *Pneumocystis* e **ausência da sombra tímica**. Vacinas vivas são contraindicadas.

cards.front: What is the classic triad of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome?
cards.back: X-linked **WAS** gene defect (actin cytoskeleton). Triad: **thrombocytopenia with small platelets** (bleeding), **eczema** and **recurrent infections**. IgM is low; IgA and IgE are often high. Risk of autoimmune disease and **lymphoma**.
cards.back_pt: Defeito, ligado ao X, do gene **WAS** (citoesqueleto de actina). Tríade: **plaquetopenia com plaquetas pequenas** (sangramento), **eczema** e **infecções recorrentes**. A IgM é baixa; IgA e IgE costumam estar altas. Risco de doença autoimune e **linfoma**.

cards.front: What defect causes leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1, and what are its clues?
cards.back: Autosomal recessive loss of **CD18** (β2 integrin), so neutrophils cannot bind firmly to endothelium and leave vessels. Clues: **delayed umbilical cord separation**, omphalitis, bacterial infections **without pus**, very high blood neutrophil count, periodontitis and poor wound healing.
cards.back_pt: Perda autossômica recessiva do **CD18** (integrina β2); os neutrófilos não aderem firmemente ao endotélio nem saem dos vasos. Pistas: **queda tardia do coto umbilical**, onfalite, infecções bacterianas **sem pus**, neutrofilia acentuada no sangue, periodontite e cicatrização ruim.

questions.stem: A 10-month-old boy has had three episodes of otitis media and one pneumonia since he was 7 months old. Cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. His growth and development have been normal. A maternal uncle died of meningitis as a child. On exam, the tonsils are barely visible and no lymph nodes are palpable. Serum IgG, IgA and IgM are all very low. Flow cytometry shows normal numbers of CD3+ T cells and almost no CD19+ B cells. Which protein is most likely defective?
choices: Common γ chain of the IL-2 receptor
questions.explanation: Recurrent infections with **encapsulated bacteria** starting after maternal IgG fades, an X-linked family history, very low levels of all antibodies and **absent B cells** point to **X-linked agammaglobulinemia** (**BTK** defect). CD40 ligand deficiency is also X-linked, but B cells are present and IgM is normal or high. The IL-2 receptor γ chain defect and ADA deficiency cause SCID, with absent T cells and opportunistic infections.
questions.explanation_pt: Infecções recorrentes por **bactérias encapsuladas** que começam quando a IgG materna desaparece, história familiar ligada ao X, níveis muito baixos de todos os anticorpos e **ausência de linfócitos B** indicam **agamaglobulinemia ligada ao X** (defeito da **BTK**). A deficiência do ligante de CD40 também é ligada ao X, mas os linfócitos B estão presentes e a IgM é normal ou alta. O defeito da cadeia γ do receptor de IL-2 e a deficiência de ADA causam SCID, com ausência de linfócitos T e infecções oportunistas.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy is admitted with a liver abscess. Pus drained from the abscess grows Staphylococcus aureus. At age 2 he had Serratia marcescens lymphadenitis that needed surgical drainage, and last year he had pneumonia caused by Aspergillus fumigatus. A lymph node biopsy from that time showed granulomas. His neutrophil count is normal and neutrophils look normal on the blood smear. Which test is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?
choices: Dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry after neutrophil stimulation
Flow cytometry for CD18 on neutrophils
Peripheral smear review for giant cytoplasmic granules
questions.explanation: Abscesses and granulomas caused by **catalase-positive** organisms (*S. aureus*, *Serratia*, *Aspergillus*) suggest **chronic granulomatous disease**: phagocytes lack **NADPH oxidase** and cannot make a respiratory burst. The **DHR test** shows no fluorescence after stimulation (in the older **nitroblue tetrazolium** test, the cells stay yellow instead of turning blue). CD18 flow cytometry is the test for leukocyte adhesion deficiency, but there the infections form **no pus** and neutrophils are very high, while this boy has drainable abscesses and a normal neutrophil count.
questions.explanation_pt: Abscessos e granulomas por organismos **catalase-positivos** (*S. aureus*, *Serratia*, *Aspergillus*) sugerem **doença granulomatosa crônica (DGC)**: os fagócitos não têm **NADPH oxidase** e não fazem a explosão respiratória. O **teste da di-hidrorodamina (DHR)** não mostra fluorescência após a estimulação (no teste mais antigo do **nitroazul de tetrazólio (NBT)**, as células continuam amarelas em vez de ficarem azuis). A citometria para CD18 é o teste da deficiência de adesão leucocitária, mas nela as infecções **não formam pus** e os neutrófilos ficam muito altos, enquanto este menino tem abscessos drenáveis e contagem de neutrófilos normal.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old girl has fever, weight loss and enlarged lymph nodes. Lymph node biopsy shows Mycobacterium avium complex. At age 1 she had Salmonella bacteremia without a clear source. As an infant, she developed a spreading infection at the site of her BCG vaccine. HIV testing is negative. Serum immunoglobulins and blood counts are normal. She has never had skin or organ abscesses, and a dihydrorhodamine (DHR) test of her neutrophils is normal. A defect in which molecule best explains her infections?
questions.explanation: Disseminated **BCG**, **nontuberculous mycobacteria** and ***Salmonella*** in an HIV-negative child point to a defect in the **IL-12/IFN-γ axis**. Without IFN-γ signaling, macrophages cannot kill intracellular microbes. Chronic granulomatous disease can also cause BCG complications and *Salmonella* infection, but it causes abscesses from *S. aureus*, *Serratia* and *Aspergillus*, and the normal **DHR test** excludes it here. Disseminated **nontuberculous mycobacteria** are the key clue to the IFN-γ pathway.
questions.explanation_pt: **BCG** disseminado, **micobactérias não tuberculosas** e ***Salmonella*** em uma criança HIV-negativa indicam defeito no **eixo IL-12/IFN-γ**. Sem a sinalização do IFN-γ, os macrófagos não conseguem matar micróbios intracelulares. A doença granulomatosa crônica também pode causar complicações do BCG e infecção por *Salmonella*, mas causa abscessos por *S. aureus*, *Serratia* e *Aspergillus*, e o **teste da DHR** normal a exclui aqui. **Micobactérias não tuberculosas** disseminadas são a pista principal para a via do IFN-γ.

questions.stem: A 5-month-old boy has persistent oral thrush, chronic diarrhea and poor weight gain. He is now admitted with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Two of his mother's brothers died in infancy from infections. Chest x-ray shows no thymic shadow. Serum calcium is normal and an echocardiogram is normal. Flow cytometry shows almost no T cells and no NK cells, while B cell numbers are normal. Which protein is most likely defective?
choices: Common γ chain of the IL-2 receptor
questions.explanation: Thrush, diarrhea, failure to thrive and *Pneumocystis* in early infancy with **no thymic shadow** mean **SCID**. The X-linked pattern and the profile **T−, NK−, B+** fit a defect in the **common γ chain** shared by the receptors for IL-2, IL-7 and IL-15. **ADA deficiency** also causes SCID, but it is autosomal recessive and the toxic deoxyadenosine metabolites (dATP) also kill **B cells**. Normal calcium and heart argue against DiGeorge syndrome.
questions.explanation_pt: Candidíase oral, diarreia, déficit de crescimento e *Pneumocystis* no início da vida, com **ausência da sombra tímica**, indicam **SCID**. O padrão ligado ao X e o perfil **T−, NK−, B+** correspondem a um defeito da **cadeia γ comum**, compartilhada pelos receptores de IL-2, IL-7 e IL-15. A **deficiência de ADA** também causa SCID, mas é autossômica recessiva e os metabólitos tóxicos da desoxiadenosina (dATP) também matam os **linfócitos B**. Cálcio e coração normais falam contra a síndrome de DiGeorge.

notes.title: Immunodeficiency: reading the infection pattern
notes.body_md:
## Infection pattern points to the defect

- **Encapsulated bacteria**, sinopulmonary infections, *Giardia*: **antibody** defect (also asplenia, early complement).
- **Viruses, fungi, *Pneumocystis*, intracellular microbes**: **T-cell** defect.
- **Catalase-positive** bacteria, *Aspergillus*, skin abscesses, gingivitis: **phagocyte** defect.
- Recurrent ***Neisseria***: terminal complement (**C5-C9**); see the innate immunity block.

## B-cell defects

- **X-linked agammaglobulinemia** (**BTK**): no B cells, all Ig low, onset after ~6 months.
- **CVID**: B cells present, no plasma cells; later onset; autoimmunity, lymphoma.
- **Selective IgA deficiency**: the most common primary immunodeficiency; often silent; mucosal infections, **anaphylaxis** to blood products (see transfusion block), false-negative IgA celiac tests.
- **Hyper-IgM** (**CD40L**): no class switching; also *Pneumocystis* and *Cryptosporidium*.

## T-cell defects

- **DiGeorge** (22q11.2): thymic hypoplasia or aplasia, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects (see genetics and parathyroid blocks).
- **IL-12/IFN-γ receptor defects**: mycobacteria and *Salmonella*.
- **Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis**: T-cell (Th17) failure against *Candida* in skin, nails and mucosa.
- **Hyper-IgE** (**STAT3**): cold staphylococcal abscesses, retained teeth, eczema.

## Combined defects

- **SCID**: IL-2 receptor **γ chain** (X-linked) or **ADA** (see nucleotide metabolism block); no thymic shadow; stem cell transplant.
- **Wiskott-Aldrich** (**WAS**): small platelets, eczema, infections.
- **Ataxia-telangiectasia** (**ATM**): see molecular biology block.

## Phagocyte defects

- **CGD**: no **NADPH oxidase**; **DHR** or NBT test.
- **LAD-1** (**CD18**): late cord separation, no pus.
- **Chédiak-Higashi** (**LYST**): see cell biology block.

## Secondary immunodeficiency

- **Malnutrition**: the most common cause worldwide.
- **Splenectomy** or sickle cell disease: encapsulated bacteria.
- **Drugs**: glucocorticoids, chemotherapy, transplant immunosuppressants, biologics.
- **HIV**: loss of CD4+ T cells (see microbiology).
- Diabetes, chronic kidney disease, old age.

## Rule

- Avoid **live vaccines** in severe T-cell or combined defects.
notes.body_pt_md:
## O padrão de infecção indica o defeito

- **Bactérias encapsuladas**, infecções sinopulmonares, *Giardia*: defeito de **anticorpos** (também asplenia, complemento inicial).
- **Vírus, fungos, *Pneumocystis*, micróbios intracelulares**: defeito de **linfócitos T**.
- Bactérias **catalase-positivas**, *Aspergillus*, abscessos cutâneos, gengivite: defeito de **fagócitos**.
- ***Neisseria*** recorrente: complemento terminal (**C5-C9**); ver o bloco de imunidade inata.

## Defeitos de linfócitos B

- **Agamaglobulinemia ligada ao X** (**BTK**): sem linfócitos B, todas as Ig baixas, início após ~6 meses.
- **IDCV**: linfócitos B presentes, sem plasmócitos; início mais tardio; autoimunidade, linfoma.
- **Deficiência seletiva de IgA**: a imunodeficiência primária mais comum; muitas vezes silenciosa; infecções de mucosas, **anafilaxia** a hemoderivados (ver bloco de transfusão), testes de IgA para doença celíaca falsamente negativos.
- **Hiper-IgM** (**CD40L**): sem troca de classe; também *Pneumocystis* e *Cryptosporidium*.

## Defeitos de linfócitos T

- **DiGeorge** (22q11.2): hipoplasia ou aplasia tímica, hipocalcemia, defeitos conotruncais (ver blocos de genética e paratireoide).
- **Defeitos dos receptores de IL-12/IFN-γ**: micobactérias e *Salmonella*.
- **Candidíase mucocutânea crônica**: falha dos linfócitos T (Th17) contra *Candida* na pele, unhas e mucosas.
- **Hiper-IgE** (**STAT3**): abscessos estafilocócicos frios, retenção dentária, eczema.

## Defeitos combinados

- **SCID** (imunodeficiência combinada grave): **cadeia γ** do receptor de IL-2 (ligada ao X) ou **ADA** (ver bloco de metabolismo dos nucleotídeos); sem sombra tímica; transplante de células-tronco hematopoéticas.
- **Wiskott-Aldrich** (**WAS**): plaquetas pequenas, eczema, infecções.
- **Ataxia-telangiectasia** (**ATM**): ver bloco de biologia molecular.

## Defeitos de fagócitos

- **DGC**: sem **NADPH oxidase**; teste de **DHR** ou NBT.
- **LAD-1** (**CD18**): queda tardia do coto umbilical, sem pus.
- **Chédiak-Higashi** (**LYST**): ver bloco de biologia celular.

## Imunodeficiência secundária

- **Desnutrição**: a causa mais comum no mundo.
- **Esplenectomia** ou doença falciforme: bactérias encapsuladas.
- **Medicamentos**: glicocorticoides, quimioterapia, imunossupressores de transplante, biológicos.
- **HIV**: perda de linfócitos T CD4+ (ver microbiologia).
- Diabetes, doença renal crônica, idade avançada.

## Regra

- Evitar **vacinas vivas** nos defeitos graves de linfócitos T ou combinados.
